newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas futures finish lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas futures finish lower on profit taking.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures settled mostly lower Tuesday after some early profit taking took the steam out of the rally, industry sources said.
January settled 29.7 cents lower at $4.17 per million British thermal units after trading in a $4.06-4.50 range. February was down 27.1 cents at $3.613, stretching its discount to Jan to 55.7 cents.
"The market was definitely overdone. We should test that $4.05-4.06 area again tomorrow," one futures source said, noting next week's forecast is calling for normal temperatures along the East Coast.
Technical traders said January support was still at $4.05, then in the $3.87-4.05 gap. Resistance was pegged in the $4.56-4.60 area. The contract high is $4.60.
NYMEX said 44,325 Hub contracts traded, down from Monday's revised tally of 46,719. Open interest for December 16 rose another 4,038 to 160,308, which is just under the year's high.
Because of this, some traders said that the market's move past the contract high before its expiry next Tuesday is unlikely.

In the cash market, Gulf Coast gas traded mostly in the $4.40-4.45 area, up more than 40 cents from Monday. Midcontinent prices were higher in the low-$4.60s, while Permian basin prices were talked mostly in the low-$4.80s.
NYMEX January Alberta natgas was untraded but settled 2.5 cents lower at $1.725.
Open interest for December 16 was up 9 to 240.
Physical December prices at the AECO storage hub were slightly softer in the C$2.03-2.08 per gigajoule, or low-$1.60s per mmBtu range. January prices were talked around $1.70 per mmBtu.
NYMEX Permian natgas was untraded for the fourteenth consecutive day, with January settling at $3.70, down 32 cents.
Permian open interest for December 16 was unchanged at 89.
On the KCBT, January finished 20 cents lower at $4.10. Open interest for December 16 fell by 133 to 2,864. The East/West spread was at seven cents (NYMEX premium).
